title: The model method: bar models for word problems
subject: math

objectives.text: Draw a bar model with unit boxes that are all the same length and check that bars are to scale
successCriteria: I can draw Mia's 2 unit boxes and Ben's 3 unit boxes so that every unit box is the same length
I can check that a 2-unit bar is exactly twice a 1-unit bar
assessmentPoints: Unit answers in the opening activity
Responses when the bars-must-be-to-scale trap is sprung in the fourth activity

objectives.text: Use a before-and-after model to show what changed and a part-whole model to split a whole bar and find a difference
successCriteria: I can show Mia's 3 units before, 1 unit given away and 2 units after
I can split a whole bar of 7 units into 3 units of boys and 4 units of girls and find the difference of 1 unit
assessmentPoints: Before-and-after answers in the second activity
Worksheet answers in the closing practice

activities.title: Line the unit bars up: every unit the same length

differentiation.support: Provide a pre-drawn whole bar split into 7 equal units so learners can mark the 3 units of boys before reading off the girls.

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain why a bar model with guessed unit lengths cannot be trusted to compare amounts.
